# tiedliene

State differencing, patching, cloning, and undo/redo management for JavaScript objects.

## Diff types

A diff is an array of changes. Each change has a `type` (`'add'`, `'set'`, or `'delete'`), a string-array `path`, and the applicable `old` and `new` values.

## `determineDiff`

```TypeScript
determineDiff(
  before: Record<string, any>,
  after: Record<string, any>,
  path?: string[],
): Change[]
```

Returns the changes needed to transform `before` into `after`.

## `applyDiff`

```TypeScript
applyDiff(state: Record<string, any>, diff: Change[]): Record<string, any>
```

Validates and applies changes to `state`, then returns that state. Invalid paths fail atomically.

## `revertDiff`

```TypeScript
revertDiff(state: Record<string, any>, diff: Change[]): Record<string, any>
```

Applies the inverse of the changes and returns the restored state.

## `cloneRecursive`

```TypeScript
cloneRecursive(value: any, clones?: WeakMap<object, any>): any
```

Deeply clones supported values while preserving cycles and shared references.

## `manageState`

```TypeScript
manageState(
  initialState: Record<string, any>,
  options?: {
    maximumHistory?: number,
    snapshot?: 'clone' | 'reference',
    clone?: (value: any) => any,
  },
): {
  get: () => Record<string, any>,
  set: (state: Record<string, any>) => void,
  undo: () => void,
  redo: () => void,
}
```

Creates an undoable state manager. `maximumHistory` defaults to `50`, with `0` disabling history. `snapshot` defaults to `'clone'`; use `'reference'` only when callers will treat returned state as immutable.

Plain objects and arrays can contain cycles. `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, and typed arrays are treated as atomic values. Functions, custom instances, weak collections, DOM nodes, symbol-keyed state, and enumerable accessors are rejected.

## Example

```JavaScript
import { applyDiff, determineDiff } from '@doars/tiedliene'

const state = { count: 1 }
const diff = determineDiff(state, { count: 2 })
applyDiff(state, diff)
```
